eyebrow: Watsi · NYC Bryant Park · 22 Sep 2026 · Street compilation
title: Street compilation:
title_q: “Would You Help Someone You've Never Met?”
length: about 95 s (about 80 s with the three lifts)
headline: Strangers say yes, then 30 seconds later they really fund a stranger's surgery on their phone.
story: Most street videos collect answers. This one lets people act on theirs. Nick asks strangers in Bryant Park: would you help someone you've never met? They say yes. Then he hands them a $10 Watsi card and they pick a real patient on their phone.

Keep the skeptics: Paul asks “is there some kind of catch” and Jai and Josephine point out that much of the world has free healthcare. That makes the yes answers true. It ends on Maria: “you never know when it's going to be you.” Light, quick, hopeful.
do: Open on Gori's line on frame 1. Candid footage, no board, no logo.
Every yes leads to a card and a real patient pick.
Keep both skeptics and their turn.
Name supers large, first name only, after 0:05.
Blur every readable card or phone code.
dont: No Julius in this cut. He has his own video.
No name super for the man who picks Da.
No extra detail about the patients beyond what people say.

FX3 lav, multi-mono, 2 channels per file. Use the live channel and map it to both sides. On Julius's clip from the same day, channel 1 was the lav. Check each person on the waveform. (Not measured for these clips: the Drive download limit stopped the audio check.)
−14 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP peak. Match every person's level: the clips were shot in different spots.
Lato Bold, white, soft shadow, large. Pop word by word. No highlight box, no shading block. One line at a time. Always on screen, also in pauses. Keep the bottom 20% clear for app buttons.

checklist: Read every caption against the audio. The transcript labels the speakers wrong: go by the voice.
Watsi is spelled with a capital W only. Never “WOTC”.
No card or phone code is readable in any frame.
Name supers are large, first name only, never before 0:05. No super for the man who picks Da.
Patients are captioned exactly as the strangers say them. No extra text.
Captions never drop out between people.
End card: “Tell us your story.” then watsi.org/who-gives, lowercase.

decisions.b: The brief asks for 60–75 s, but every person it chose only fits at about 95 s. The three “Lift” rows (Maddie, Zane, the Jai turn) take it to about 80 s. Nick decides which version goes to V1.
End card: watsi.org, or the Who Gives close, “Tell us your story.” + watsi.org/who-gives (planned)? This cut uses the Who Gives look and the 6 Oct direction asks for that card. Confirm.
Production Planning row 12949181905 still says Reference = Requested, owner Nick. Sonam suggested givewithjose.com on 15 Sep. A producer has to pick it.

client_note: Why this matters: Sonam said edits feel flat when there is no real person at the center. Here every beat is a real stranger acting, not just talking. Keep it quick and keep the payoff.
